survey: Image 5 is a folding camp armchair seen in three-quarter view from the front left. Green fabric is stretched between two grey tube back uprights to make the backrest. The seat sling runs between hinge points at the four seat corners, each with a round pivot cap. The front legs form an X with one central pivot bolt, and each tube runs from a top seat-corner hinge to the foot on the opposite side. The left side frame runs from the rear-left seat hinge down to the back-left foot. Three grey rubber feet touch the floor and sit in the cast shadow. The fourth, rear-right foot is plausibly hidden behind the frame. Each orange armrest sits on a curved tube post. The left post drops to the front-left seat hinge. The right post curves down to the right seat edge, and the armrest's rear end meets the right back upright beside the backrest. Every tube starts and ends at a hinge, foot or armrest, so nothing floats. The X can pivot to fold, the fabric could carry a sitter, and no parts are invented. The frame is simplified compared with a real quad chair, but it stays consistent.
